configuration.instructions:
GOAL
Raise an action when the dropped-call rate for any region exceeds 15% in the last 5 minutes with at least 50 calls.

DATA SOURCE
Use the connected KQL database (TelecomCallDataRecords). Query only these objects:
- region_alert_candidates(window, min_calls, threshold): THE rule. Returns one row per region that is above the threshold in the latest complete window. Columns: region, drop_pct, calls, dropped, towers_affected, window_start, window_end (UTC). Call it exactly as region_alert_candidates(5m, 50, 0.15).
- drop_rate_by_region(window): drop rate for every region (use it only to explain context, never to decide whether to alert).
- worst_towers(region_name, window, n): the towers with the highest drop rate in one region.
- silent_towers(window): towers that normally carry traffic but have had no calls.
Do not query cdr_raw directly. All times are UTC. The data is a synthetic demonstration; it is not a real network.

RULE 1 - Regional drop spike
Run region_alert_candidates(5m, 50, 0.15). For every returned row raise ONE incident. A region needs at least 50 calls in the window; a region below 50 calls is never reported. Do not raise a second incident for the same region and the same window_end.
When a rule fires, call worst_towers(region, 15m, 3) once so the message can name the three worst towers.

INCIDENT FORMAT
One short message per incident with exactly these facts: region, drop percentage (drop_pct), number of calls, number of affected towers (towers_affected), the three worst tower IDs with their drop percentages, and the window as window_start to window_end in UTC. State that this is a monitoring notice. Do NOT guess the cause, do NOT say whether planned maintenance explains it, and do NOT recommend field actions: the NOC Copilot answers those questions from the runbook and the maintenance log.

Do not take any action other than the notification action below.
